newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt launches campaign to restart Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Egypt launches campaign to restart Mideast peace.

text.p: Egypt said on Monday it would launch a widespread diplomatic campaign to lobby Washington and the European Union for initiatives it hopes will salvage the faltering Middle East peace process.

Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters Egypt would take part in a flurry of diplomatic efforts which will try within the coming weeks to push forward Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations fettered by Israel's decision to build a new Jewish settlement in disputed Arab East Jerusalem.

"We will have discussions with European Union foreign ministers in Malta, (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat is here now and (presidential adviser) Osama el-Baz will go to Washington tomorrow to meet (U.S. Middle East envoy) Dennis Ross," Moussa said.
The Palestinian leader met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Monday for talks on the latest troubles facing the Middle East peace process.

"There are specific diplomatic efforts, but this isn't a substitute for real talks, it's just a springboard that takes Jerusalem and settlements into consideration. These are the essence of the talks," Moussa said after the two leaders met.
Countries attending the two-day Malta foreign ministers conference are to discuss advancing the 27-member EU-Mediterranean Partnership created in Barcelona in 1995.
Arafat is due to leave Cairo for Malta on Tuesday but Palestinian officials said he would not meet Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy there.
The Palestinians refuse to hold talks with Israel until it stops work on the 6,500-house settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim, which is also known at Har Homa in Hebrew.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the talks would not resume until Arafat cracked down on the violence which has raged in Jerusalem and the West Bank ever since construction work on the project began on March 18.

The United States, Israel's main ally and a sponsor of the peace talks, has angered Arabs by its conservative criticism of the new settlement. Washington further infuriated them when it vetoed two U.N. resolutions condemning the project.
Last week, Palestinian negotiators met with Ross in Washington to try and break the deadlock and Moussa said the U.S. envoy would hold talks with Arafat within a few days.

Asked whether the Washington talks were successful, Moussa, whose country champions the Palestinian cause, said: "I can't answer for Arafat but his position is clear. He can't accept anything on Jerusalem and the negotiations must be balanced and not based on what the Israelis have offered in the past months."

Egypt and the Palestinians have in the past turned to the EU to balance out what they see as U.S. bias towards Israel. But Netanyahu has refused many EU initiatives and commentators say Levy is afraid Arabs would use the Malta conference to criticise the settlement policy.
EU council president Hans van Mierlo said the issue would not be brought up during the two-day meeting but Moussa said the Middle East peace process would overshadow the two-day meet.
"The peace process is not on the agenda but it is there looming in the air, it's in the climate... and we the Mediterraneans cannot not be affected," Moussa said.

The 15-member EU, seeking a more active role in the region, suggested last week both sides abstain from unilateral action and said Israel should freeze settlement building. Egypt said the initiative was lacking and Netanyahu rejected it totally.
